core_obligations: Derive part (1) from part (2) together with the fact that zero-dimensional connected components of X are spectra of fields (proof lines 6086-6087).

Reduce to irreducible components: f maps each irreducible component Z into itself, f|_Z is again an automorphism fixing every point, and reducedness lets the whole problem be checked on each Z (proof lines 6090-6095).
Reduce from X to a nonempty affine open U, which intersects the component in a scheme-theoretically dense open, so it suffices to prove f|_U is the identity (proof lines 6098-6101).

In the affine case over an infinite field, show S = union of V(g - lambda) over lambda in k is dense, that f^sharp fixes g(x) at each x in S, and by reducedness and density conclude g = f^sharp(g), hence f^sharp = id on the whole k-algebra (proof lines 6104-6122).

In the affine case over a finite field, reduce to the one-dimensional case using the finite automorphism group of a curve, then run the analogous density argument over the closed points whose residue-field degree is prime to the order of f (proof lines 6126-6145).
proof_roadmap: Reduce part (1) to part (2) via zero-dimensional components being spectra of fields.
Pass to irreducible components and then to a scheme-theoretically dense affine open.
Over an infinite field run the V(g-lambda) density argument to show f^sharp fixes the generators g.
Over a finite field reduce to curves, use finiteness of the automorphism group, and repeat the density argument with prime-to-order degrees.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that an automorphism f of a reduced finite-type scheme over k fixing every point of the underlying topological space preserves every coherent module, and equals the identity provided every irreducible component has positive dimension. The proof is a cascade of reductions - to irreducible components, to a dense affine open, to a single affine algebra with k infinite or finite - and at each stage a density argument (the union of the V(g-lambda) for lambda in k, or the closed points with prime-to-n degree) forces g = f^sharp(g) and hence the identity (proof lines 6085-6145). H2: several independent reductions and the two field-size cases are the substance; none is written out anywhere else in the span.
